You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Internal advice – buyer side

## 1. Threshold point: the "FINAL / agreed at principal level" framing

Before the clause-by-clause review, the Seller's preamble needs to be dealt with. It asserts that (a) 10–20% caps, ~1% baskets, 12–18 month periods and buyer-knowledge qualifiers are "market standard", and (b) the positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams" and are "FINAL and not intended to be re-opened".

Under playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3, neither assertion carries weight unless confirmed through our own authority process. We have no record of Amelia Frost giving written authority on any fallback, and the Seller's own Disclosure Letter at [11] states that "no expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included". The two Seller documents are therefore inconsistent with each other on this point, which reinforces that the preamble is advocacy, not a record of agreement.

**Recommendation:** Respond that no positions have been agreed or cleared by Wattlebridge, that the draft is treated as a Seller opening mark-up in full, and that any suggestion of principal-level agreement should be evidenced in writing from our side (it will not be). Do not engage with the "market standard" argument on its merits; it is irrelevant to our playbook.

## 2. Clause-by-clause departures from playbook

### 2.1 Clause 12.1 – General warranty cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. 20% is a conditional fallback only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None given.
- **Analysis:** The fact that the Seller's number happens to equal our fallback does not make it cleared (playbook expressly says so). The Seller may know or have guessed our fallback; either way it is their proposal, not our concession.
- **Push back:** Reinstate 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Hold until and unless Amelia Frost authorises in writing by reference to this specific draft.

### 2.2 Clause 12.2 – Thresholds
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery.
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery once exceeded.
- **Analysis:** Three separate departures, each material. The de minimis is 5x ours, the basket 5x ours, and the shift to "excess only" (a deductible) rather than "tipping" (first dollar) is structurally worse than the headline numbers suggest. Combined with the knowledge exclusion and general disclosure (below), the practical recovery for a SaaS business with many small contract/data issues could be close to nil.
- **Push back:** AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / tipping basket. No fallback authority exists on any of these.

### 2.3 Clause 12.3 / 13 – Time limits and "applies to all Claims"
- **Seller:** 18 months; plus a sweeping rule that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months only with Amelia Frost written approval (none given). Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Analysis:** Two issues. The 18-month number is the same unauthorised-fallback problem as the cap. More serious is the second sentence: a default rule that every limitation applies to every Claim is precisely the "hidden general-regime override" the playbook prohibits. It would drag Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnity and covenant claims into the 18-month/20% regime by silence.
- **Push back:** 24 months for general warranties; delete the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" default entirely and replace with express, category-specific regimes.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
- **Seller:** Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Playbook:** Separate regime – 100% cap, minimum six years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- **Analysis:** This is one of the most significant departures. On the Seller's draft, if title to the shares fails, recovery is capped at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m purchase, subject to a AUD 250k deductible, lost after 18 months, and excluded if the buyer "could have discovered" the issue from public records. That is not acceptable on any view. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason.
- **Push back:** Full separate Fundamental Warranty regime per playbook. Non-negotiable.

### 2.5 Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature"
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature.
- **Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this. Categories kept separate.
- **Analysis:** "Of any nature" with no fraud carve-out means the Seller is purporting to cap and time-bar its own fraud. Apart from the policy objection, this is likely unenforceable as to fraud under NSW law in any event, but we should not rely on that – the clause must say it. The "all Claims of any nature" wording also reinforces the general-regime override in 2.3 by applying non-reliance and exclusive remedy to specific indemnities (Ironquay, bonuses, Riverlark payout) where they should not bite.
- **Push back:** Insert an express, overriding fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out applying to every limitation, exclusion, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provision. Confine 9.3/12.8/20.5 to general Warranty Claims and exclude specific indemnities, Fundamental Warranties, Tax and IP (pending resolution), payment and covenant claims.

### 2.6 Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2] – General disclosure
- **Seller:** Everything in the data room as at 22 Sept 2026 (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" is deemed disclosed.
- **Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Analysis:** Three of the three prohibited mechanisms are present. [1.2] adds "publicly searchable corporate records", which is open-ended (not limited to ASIC) and effectively imports a prudent-search standard. Note also the date: the data room is frozen at 22 September 2026, over six weeks ago; anything added since is not within the deemed disclosure, which is a point in our favour if we accept any data-room disclosure at all, but we should not.
- **Push back:** Disclosure effective only to the extent fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Delete [1.1] and [1.2]. If any data-room reference is to survive, it must be by specific document reference against a specific warranty, and the data-room index must be scheduled and frozen.

### 2.7 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".
- **Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Analysis:** This clause goes beyond actual knowledge to constructive knowledge ("discoverable"), extends to advisers, and has no carve-outs. Read with [1.1]/[1.2], it would mean effectively any matter in the data room or on any public register is both disclosed and barred. It would also bar claims on title and on the Ironquay/bonus matters, which the Seller itself has told us about – the Seller's own disclosures become a shield.
- **Push back:** Delete 8.3. Knowledge qualifiers, if any, go the other way – on seller warranties "so far as the Seller is aware", with named persons (to be identified from Paperbark management and Harbourglass) and a reasonable-enquiry standard.

### 2.8 Clauses 3 / 6.3 – Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter [2] confirms no final written consent and no evidence of satisfied conditions as at 22 Sept.
- **Playbook:** Effective consent AND evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer.
- **Analysis:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue. A consent "satisfied on delivery" of a document that may itself be conditional (clause 11.3) is not an effective consent; it transfers the conditions risk to us. The Seller's own [2] is a verified update that the gap is real and current as at the letter date – we should refresh it (ask whether anything has moved since 22 Sept) rather than assume either way.
- **Push back:** Condition precedent: unconditional written consent from Bluefen under 11.2 in agreed form, together with evidence satisfactory to the Buyer (acting reasonably) that each 11.3 condition has been satisfied or waived, delivered before Completion. Seller obligation at least "all reasonable endeavours" with specified steps; Buyer right to terminate if not satisfied by the end date. Consider a price-protection mechanism (retention/escrow or revenue-based adjustment) if the Seller will not accept a hard CP.

### 2.9 Clauses 2 / 7 – Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion". Disclosure Letter [3]: not repaid; no discharge included.
- **Playbook:** Current payout letter; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases at Completion. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval.
- **Analysis:** On the Seller's draft we would pay AUD 24m for a company that remains encumbered and indebted to its bank at Completion, with only a promise of a later release. The debt-free/cash-free basis is undermined, and the DD-003 change-of-control clause (8.1) means Completion itself may be an event of default if not addressed in advance. The figure is "approximately" – we need a dated payout.
- **Push back:** Completion deliverables: dated Riverlark payout letter; Buyer pays payout amount direct to Riverlark from Completion funds (deducted from the price under the debt-free mechanism); executed deeds of release/discharge and PPSR releases delivered at Completion, or at minimum an irrevocable bank undertaking to release on receipt of the payout. Any post-completion release structure requires Amelia Frost written approval, which we do not have – so the default position is release at Completion.

### 2.10 Funds flow – DD-005 employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. Disclosure Letter [5] confirms they do not appear in the funds flow and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Analysis:** "A matter for the Seller" is not the same as "seller-funded in the funds flow". The bonuses are payable by the Company (Paperbark) on Completion; if they are not funded, they become a liability of the business we are buying. On-costs (superannuation on the bonus, payroll tax, potentially leave accruals) could add materially – order of 15–25% is a reasonable working assumption, but we should obtain the actual figures rather than estimate.
- **Push back:** Specific funds-flow line item: AUD 420,000 plus all associated superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs, treated as Debt (or a Transaction Cost) in the price adjustment, or paid by the Seller directly before Completion with evidence. Require the Seller to state the on-cost figures. Add a specific indemnity for any bonus/on-cost amount not so funded.

### 2.11 Clause 11.1 – Ironquay IP
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; "considered adequate". Disclosure Letter [4]: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of Project Materials on payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but this is not bank verification; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- **Analysis:** The real risk is not the AUD 180,000; it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 Project Materials at all until payment clears, and we have no evidence of payment or assignment. An indemnity for the fee only does nothing if Ironquay asserts title to the IP, refuses to deliver, or claims additional sums. The Seller's own [4] confirms the evidentiary gap.
- **Push back:** (i) Completion deliverable or CP: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay of the Project Materials (the "cure"); (ii) broaden 11.1 to an indemnity for all Loss arising from any claim by Ironquay or any defect in the Company's title to, or right to use, any Ironquay-developed materials, not limited to the SOW3 fee, and outside the general cap/basket/time limits; (iii) obtain bank evidence on the AUD 180,000 rather than assuming the ledger is right in either direction.

### 2.12 Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 – DD-006 export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material". Disclosure Letter [6]: ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) sent to an unintended external address; unknown whether accessed; notification question open; investigation preliminary; no loss stated.
- **Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Analysis:** We should neither accept "not material" nor assert that it is a notifiable data breach – the record does not support either. What is unacceptable is Completion proceeding with the investigation still "preliminary" six weeks after the letter date and the Seller characterising it as closed. The data set is modest (~1,240 business-contact records) but includes activity timestamps, and the recipient is external and unknown.
- **Push back:** Pre-Completion covenants: preserve all logs and evidence; complete and document the investigation (including link-access logs, whether the link was revoked/expired, and the recipient's response); written update before signing and again before Completion; comply with any notification obligation determined to apply. Specific warranty as to the completeness of the incident disclosure. Specific indemnity for Loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory, notification costs, third-party claims), outside general limitations. Do not put a number on it in either direction.

### 2.13 Supplier renewals – Sandbar (AUD 330,000)
- **Seller:** "Ordinary-course operating costs". Disclosure Letter [8]: three renewals of AUD 110,000 each; silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Analysis:** The Seller's "ordinary-course" characterisation is not supported by its own [8], which expressly declines to say so. Equally, the playbook does not direct us to treat them as Debt. The questions are timing (do they fall due pre- or post-Completion / within the locked-box or completion-accounts period), whether they were accrued, and whether the three are genuinely related (DD-008 and DD-011 read together).
- **Push back:** Information request: copies of all three renewal terms, due dates, termination rights, and accounting treatment. Decide classification once answered. Meanwhile, ensure the price-adjustment definitions do not pre-empt the answer (e.g. by an "ordinary course" exclusion that would bite on these).

### 2.14 Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime"
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime.
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution; keep categories separate.
- **Analysis:** This is the Seller attempting to close two open categories by assertion and fold them into the 20%/18-month regime. Nothing has been settled. We are not instructed to demand unlimited tax liability, but we are instructed not to let Tax and IP default into the general regime.
- **Push back:** State expressly that Tax and IP remain open. Reserve a separate Tax Indemnity/Tax Warranty regime and a separate IP warranty regime with their own cap and period, to be negotiated. Ensure the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" default (2.3 above) does not capture them in the interim.

### 2.15 Title – DD-012 share register
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. Disclosure Letter [10]: identifies the source relied on; does not state the Buyer has verified.
- **Playbook:** Require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Analysis:** The register is maintained by the Company (i.e. by the Seller's side). It is evidence of what the Company records, not independent proof of title, and it says nothing about encumbrances (note the Riverlark security – is there a share mortgage?), options, pre-emptive rights or the Seller's own authority.
- **Push back:** Independent verification: current ASIC extract and historical company search; PPSR search against the Company and the Seller (specifically for any security over the shares in favour of Riverlark); Seller board/shareholder resolutions and constitutional authority; confirmation of no options, convertibles or pre-emptive rights; full Fundamental Warranties on title, capacity and authority under the separate regime in 2.4.

### 2.16 Lesser points noted (no departure, but monitor)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** Notification only, not consent, per [7]. Include a pre-Completion covenant to give the notice and evidence it.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Assignment restriction; not triggered by share sale per [9]. Confirm by our own reading of the clause rather than relying on the Seller's characterisation; check for any change-of-control limb.
- **Disclosure Letter [1.4] (no admission):** Standard and acceptable in itself, but it should not be allowed to undercut the specific indemnities we are seeking.
- **Data-room cut-off (22 Sept 2026):** Over six weeks old. Request a refreshed index and a bring-down of all specific disclosures at signing and at Completion.

## 3. Interaction effects

The Seller's package should be read as a system, not as separate clauses. The combination of (a) whole-data-room and public-record deemed disclosure, (b) a constructive-knowledge exclusion extending to advisers, (c) a 20% cap with a AUD 250k deductible and AUD 25k de minimis, (d) an 18-month period applying by default to all Claims, and (e) exclusive-remedy and non-reliance applying "to all Claims of any nature" with no fraud carve-out, would in practice reduce the warranty package to very limited value. Each of the specific matters the Seller has itself disclosed (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, DD-006) would arguably be both disclosed and knowledge-barred. We should present our mark-up on that basis and resist piecemeal trading.

## 4. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "FINAL / agreed" framing | Principal-level agreement asserted | Reject; no Wattlebridge authority exists; treat as opening mark-up |
| 2 | General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m; no fallback authority |
| 3 | Thresholds (12.2) | AUD 25k / AUD 250k / excess-only | AUD 5k / AUD 50k / first-dollar |
| 4 | Claims period (12.3) | 18 months | 24 months; no fallback authority |
| 5 | "All Claims" default (13) | Limitations apply to all Claims unless stated | Delete; express category-specific regimes |
| 6 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | Separate: 100% cap, 6+ years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge |
| 7 | Fraud carve-out (9.3/12.8/20.5) | None; "all Claims of any nature" | Overriding carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct |
| 8 | Disclosure (Sch 7, [1.1]–[1.2]) | Data room + public records deemed disclosed | Specific fair disclosure only; delete general disclosures |
| 9 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Blanket, constructive, advisers | Delete |
| 10 | Bluefen (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | CP: unconditional consent + evidence 11.3 conditions met, pre-Completion |
| 11 | Riverlark (2/7) | Post-Completion release | Payout letter, direct repayment from funds, releases at Completion |
| 12 | DD-005 bonuses | Not itemised; "matter for Seller" | Specific line item incl. on-costs, or seller-funded with evidence; indemnity |
| 13 | Ironquay (11.1) | SOW3 fee only | Payment evidence + confirmatory assignment; broadened IP indemnity |
| 14 | DD-006 incident (4.6/Sch 6) | "Not material" | Preserve logs, complete investigation, updates, specific indemnity; no number either way |
| 15 | Sandbar renewals | "Ordinary course" | Information request; assess before classifying |
| 16 | Tax / IP | "Settled under general regime" | Remain open; separate regimes reserved |
| 17 | Title | DD-012 register | Independent ASIC/PPSR/authority evidence; Fundamental Warranties |
| 18 | Data-room staleness | Cut-off 22 Sept 2026 | Refreshed index; bring-down at signing and Completion |

**Immediate actions:**
1. Written response to Harbourglass counsel rejecting the "agreed/FINAL" characterisation and confirming that all positions remain open.
2. Issue a full buyer mark-up on the basis above.
3. Information requests: Riverlark payout and security documents; Bluefen consent status post-22 Sept and 11.3 conditions; Ironquay payment/assignment evidence and bank confirmation of the AUD 180,000; bonus on-cost figures; DD-006 investigation status and logs; Sandbar renewal terms; ASIC/PPSR searches (we should run these ourselves).
4. Internal: confirm with Amelia Frost that no fallback authority has been or will be given on the cap or claims period at this stage, so the deal team holds the 25% / 24-month line consistently.
=== END ADVICE ===
